analysis.investment_thesis: Happiest Minds has a compelling 23% revenue CAGR and a timely Gen AI pivot, but net profit declined 25% YoY (₹248→₹185 Cr) while borrowings nearly tripled (₹512→₹1,274 Cr), destroying the clean growth story. At P/E 28x with earnings actually contracting, the PEG is effectively undefined — this is not the price I want to pay for a deteriorating margin profile.
key_strengths: Consistent 23% revenue CAGR over 6 years (₹590→₹2,061 Cr) with dedicated Gen AI segment (GBS) riding a genuine secular tailwind
OCF positive all 5 years; FY25 FCF of ₹225 Cr confirms the underlying business generates real cash
Reasonable D/E of 0.28 on book basis — though that number is rapidly deteriorating with fresh debt issuance
key_risks: Net profit collapsed 25% YoY (₹248→₹185 Cr) despite 27% revenue growth — finance costs nearly tripled to ₹99 Cr, signaling debt-funded acquisitions are eating earnings
Borrowings exploded from ₹512 Cr (FY24) to ₹1,274 Cr (FY25), a 2.5x jump in one year — this is a red flag for a mid-cap IT services company
Operating income barely moved (₹336→₹354 Cr, +5%) on 27% revenue growth — severe margin compression signals pricing pressure or bloated cost structure
red_flags: Earnings DECLINING while revenue grows — the classic warning sign that growth is being bought, not earned
Finance costs surged 135% YoY (₹42→₹99 Cr) — debt servicing is the primary reason profits fell
ROE of only 12.6% is barely above my floor and is trending lower as equity dilutes and profits shrink
Investing CF of -₹731 Cr with no proportionate EBITDA acceleration suggests acquisition risk — what are they buying and at what price?
analysis.detailed_analysis:
As Peter Lynch, I look for fast growers where the story is simple, the numbers confirm it, and the price is reasonable. Happiest Minds used to tell a clean story: a digitally-native IT firm compounding revenue at 23% with operating leverage. But FY25 broke that story. Revenue grew 27% to ₹2,061 Cr — impressive. Yet net profit fell from ₹248 Cr to ₹185 Cr, a 25% DROP. That's not a growth stock; that's a company spending its way into trouble. Finance costs alone hit ₹99 Cr, almost triple the prior year, as borrowings ballooned to ₹1,274 Cr. When I see debt tripling in a single year in a services business with no hard assets, I get very nervous. The "story" is now clouded by an acquisition binge.

The Gen AI angle (GBS segment) is legitimately interesting — this is a real tailwind I can observe from the market. But at P/E 28x on DECLINING earnings, the PEG ratio is effectively undefined or negative, the exact opposite of what I want. Forward P/E of 19x implies the market expects a sharp earnings rebound — possible if acquisitions integrate well, but that's a hope, not a fact. With ROE at a thin 12.6%, operating margins at 14.5% (low for Indian IT), and margin direction clearly downward, I'd rather watch this from the sidelines. If earnings recover to ₹250+ Cr and the debt story stabilizes, revisit at a lower price. Not today at ₹382.
